title: The census's independent sample agrees with its outcomes, and the kb is tagged census-<date> for a date after 2026-10-20
goal: kbgit.py tag-census tags the kb census-<date> for the census of ST-zpe7qxtv, dated after 2026-10-20

run:
import subprocess, sys
r = subprocess.run(['git', 'tag', '-l', 'census-*'], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
tags = [t for t in r.stdout.split() if t > 'census-2026-10-20']
print('census tags after 2026-10-20:', tags or 'none'); sys.exit(0 if tags else 1)

notes: Phase 4 of /kb-census from the main checkout: census.py sample --brief, a fresh checker on its brief, fixes and a resample with another seed, then kbgit.py tag-census. The tag is pushed only when the operator asks. If a source a fact cites is left unconfirmed the tag is not made: what is left is filed as backlog items and this story stays open. Premise on 2026-10-20 (the first check fails): the only census tag is census-2026-09-26. 2026-10-20 planning: the goal states what its check reads. The work is phase 4 of /kb-census: census.py sample of the changed, judged and confirmed sources, a fresh checker that did no phase-2 reading judges them, every disagreement fixed and resampled with another seed, then the tag only when no source a fact cites is left unconfirmed; the sources only front matter or ledger notes cite are filed as one backlog story. check.py passes before the work and must stay passing: it pins the kb's structure rules across the rewrites (2026-10-20 planning).
